summary: NDR feed s090_single is degraded: 52.3% of TCP sessions (69/132) are one-way, violating NDR requirement for bidirectional traffic. All other visibility checks (duplicates, VLANs, encryption, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction per TCP session to this NDR port. Most likely separate TAP/SPAN inputs for client->server and server->client are not aggregated to the same tool port, or flow-aware distribution is hashing directions to different outputs, or a SPAN is configured unidirectionally. With asymmetric routing this leaves 52.3% of sessions without return traffic at the NDR.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs_both_directions=true to reassemble TCP, track state, and detect C2/lateral movement/data exfiltration. With >50% one-way sessions it cannot see handshakes and request/response pairs, causing missed detections, broken stream reassembly, and high false-negative rate.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR tool port using bidirectional 5-tuple flow-aware hashing/aggregation so every TCP session is delivered intact for full reassembly and detection.
